note: steps 1 and 4 train a standard C-SVM with kernel k and penalty C
step 1 extracts the support vector set S = {x_i : alpha_i > 0}
sound because the SVM solution depends only on its support vectors, so retraining on S loses nothing
applies the invariance transforms L_t to each support vector to make virtual examples
starts from an admissible kernel with Gram entries K_ij = k(x_i,x_j)
picks the jitter minimizing the feature-space distance K_ii - 2K_ij + K_jj, computed by the kernel trick
the jittered forms of x_i are its invariance transforms plus itself
proof reads k(z,e_i) = <Phi(z),Phi(e_i)> through the Aronszajn feature map
expands z in an orthonormal basis, each coordinate an inner product
the target Psi = sum alpha_j Phi(x_j) is the expansion a kernel algorithm returns
iterates the Gaussian kernel exp(-|x_i-z|^2/2sigma^2), the p.d. exponential of the c.p.d. negative squared distance
the projection objective <Psi,Phi(z)> evaluates as the kernel expansion sum alpha_i k(x_i,z)
the vector to invert is typically the kernel-PCA projection P_n Phi(x) onto the top eigendirections
P_n Phi(x) is the best rank-n mean-square approximation, so a good approximate pre-image exists (denoising)
approximates the representer-type expansion Psi = sum alpha_i Phi(x_i) of a trained machine
the objective |Psi - sum beta_i Phi(z_i)|^2 is fully expressible in the Gram blocks K^z and K^zx
the minimizer makes the residual orthogonal to each Phi(z_j), the orthogonal-projection characterization
step 2 finds each one-term pre-image of the residual by the fixed-point iteration
step 3 recomputes all coefficients by the optimal-coefficient formula
compresses the machine's expansion sum alpha_i k(x_i,.) into N_z far fewer terms
